hot.title: AdaJEPA: An Adaptive Latent World Model
hot.summary: AdaJEPA introduces an adaptive latent world model that continuously recalibrates its predictions during deployment, improving planning success for goal-conditioned control under visual and dynamics distribution shifts. This approach significantly boosts performance, such as doubling success rates on unseen object shapes, while incurring minimal computational overhead.

hot.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind
hot.summary: The Orca project by Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence proposes "Next-State-Prediction" as a unified paradigm for general world foundation models, learning a latent world representation from multimodal data through both unconscious and conscious learning. The model demonstrates scalable learning behavior and improved performance in text generation, physically plausible image prediction, and emergent action generation across diverse downstream tasks with a frozen backbone.

hot.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
hot.summary: A speculative decoding framework named DSpark integrates semi-autoregressive generation with confidence-scheduled verification to enhance Large Language Model inference efficiency. It significantly improves per-user generation speeds and aggregate throughput in live production environments by dynamically optimizing draft quality and resource allocation.

hot.title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
hot.summary: A study of large language model adaptation via reinforcement learning finds that performance gains are primarily concentrated in a stable subset of middle transformer layers, with single-layer training sometimes recovering over 100% of full-parameter training improvements and enabling more efficient training strategies.

hot.title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent
hot.summary: The Agents-A1 project by Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory introduces a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that attains performance levels comparable to trillion-parameter models on long-horizon tasks by emphasizing agentic horizon scaling. The model notably outperformed 1T-parameter models on benchmarks like SEAL-0 (56.4) and IFBench (80.6) and demonstrated gold-medal-level results in a 12-hour machine learning optimization task.

hot.title: LeVLJEPA: End-to-End Vision-Language Pretraining Without Negatives
hot.summary: LeVLJEPA presents a non-contrastive end-to-end vision-language pretraining method that forgoes negative pairs, yielding visual encoders with enhanced dense semantic features. The approach improves performance on semantic segmentation and as a frozen backbone for vision-language models, also demonstrating batch-size invariance.

hot.title: TRIAGE: Role-Typed Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: TRIAGE is a framework that refines credit assignment in agentic reinforcement learning by introducing a four-role semantic taxonomy and an LLM-based judge to provide segment-level process rewards, addressing the limitations of sparse, outcome-only feedback. The method consistently improved success rates across ALFWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop benchmarks by up to 18.4% and reduced rollout length in completed tasks by over 10%.

hot.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
hot.summary: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) is a post-training paradigm that integrates multiple specialized capabilities, such as mathematical reasoning and instruction following, into a single Large Language Model. The method uses on-policy distillation with prompt-routed domain teachers to overcome issues like exposure bias and cross-domain interference. It achieved a normalized score of 0.9373 on Qwen3-30B-A3B and scaled effectively to a 309B-parameter industrial model.

hot.title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
hot.summary: Dual On-policy Distillation (DOPD) introduces an adaptive, dual distillation strategy to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, mitigating the "privilege illusion" observed when privileged information is used. The framework improved distillation efficiency, leading to an average 12.3-point gain for LLMs and 10.1-point gain for VLMs on challenging benchmarks.

hot.title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
hot.summary: WorldDirector, a framework from HKUST and Ant Group, allows for building controllable video world simulators by explicitly decoupling semantic motion orchestration from visual generation. This approach ensures persistent dynamic object memory, maintaining consistent visual identity and physical logic for entities even after prolonged periods outside the camera's view, and facilitates unrestricted viewpoint exploration.

hot.title: ABot-M0.5: Unified Mobility-and-Manipulation World Action Model
hot.summary: The ABot-M0.5 framework, developed by AMAP CV Lab, Alibaba Group, introduces a unified World Action Model (WAM) for mobile manipulation, explicitly addressing temporal granularity, action space heterogeneity, and train-test consistency mismatches in embodied learning. It achieved a 40.4% average task success rate on the RoboCasa365 benchmark, outperforming prior methods, and demonstrated robust real-world performance on complex tasks with limited demonstrations.

hot.title: ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics
hot.summary: ASPIRE, a collaborative effort by researchers from NVIDIA, UMich, UIUC, UC Berkeley, and CMU, introduces a continual learning system for robotics that autonomously discovers, refines, and accumulates reusable skills. The framework significantly improves task success rates across various simulation benchmarks, facilitates zero-shot generalization to novel tasks, and demonstrates effective sim-to-real transfer by reducing real-world robot programming and debugging effort.

hot.title: Seed2.0 Model Card: Towards Intelligence Frontier for Real-World Complexity
hot.summary: Bytedance Seed introduces the Seed2.0 model series (Pro/Lite/Mini), designed to handle real-world complexity and optimize user experience in production environments. The models achieve competitive and often state-of-the-art performance across multimodal, language, and agentic tasks, including scientific coding and solving Olympiad-level math problems.

hot.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
hot.summary: AUTOMEM introduces a framework enabling Large Language Models to automatically learn and optimize memory management as a cognitive skill, rather than a fixed architectural component. By iteratively refining memory structures and training a specialized memory component, the system significantly improves agent performance on long-horizon tasks, achieving 1.89x to 3.74x gains in progression rate and making open-weight models competitive with frontier proprietary systems.

hot.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI: From Foundations to Systems
hot.summary: Haggai Roitman's guide synthesizes the fragmented knowledge spanning LLM foundations, reinforcement learning, systems engineering, and agentic architectures into a unified, practical reference. It provides a comprehensive overview of established methodologies and architectural patterns to equip practitioners with the understanding needed to construct and deploy advanced AI systems.

hot.title: Next-Generation Agentic Reinforcement Learning Systems Enable Self-Evolving Agents
hot.summary: Researchers from Ant Group, HKUST, and Tsinghua University introduce a comprehensive system architecture designed to enable self-evolving LLM agents at an enterprise scale. This architecture proposes a standardized data protocol, an enterprise-grade data proxy, and a unified evolution control plane, with a prototype implementation (AREAL2.0) demonstrating online policy LLM weight updates from deployed agent interactions.

hot.title: World from Motion: Generative Dynamic Gaussian Reconstruction from Monocular Video
hot.summary: The research by Stanford University and NVIDIA presents "World from Motion," a framework that unifies geometry-driven 4D reconstruction with generative modeling to create freely renderable dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting representations from monocular video. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on DyCheck (e.g., 19.78 mPSNR) and MultiCamVideo benchmarks (e.g., 27.43 PSNR) by distilling novel views from a 4D-conditioned video generator into a refined 4D scene model.

hot.title: A Mathematical Introduction to Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Jianfeng Lu's mathematical introduction to diffusion models unifies classical sampling dynamics with modern score-based generative processes, presenting a comprehensive, proof-oriented framework. It rigorously derives core concepts like reverse-time SDEs and probability flow ODEs, provides a detailed error analysis for diffusion samplers, and extends the theoretical understanding to discrete data and inference-time control.

hot.title: FARS: A Fully Automated Research System Deployed at Scale
hot.summary: FARS, a fully automated, end-to-end AI research system, was developed to continuously generate complete research papers from ideation to manuscript completion. During an initial deployment, the system produced 166 papers, with 11.4% of reviewed outputs receiving human ratings at or above a typical conference acceptance threshold, demonstrating scalable autonomous research capabilities while highlighting areas for improvement in scientific rigor.

hot.title: Freeform Preference Learning for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: Freeform Preference Learning (FPL) enables robots to acquire nuanced behaviors by allowing humans to define and provide preferences along multiple natural-language axes, moving beyond ambiguous single binary choices. This method yielded policies that, on average, achieved a 38 percentage point higher success rate than baselines in real-world manipulation tasks and demonstrated compositional generalization and test-time steerability.

likes.title: ScaleAware-JEPA: Latent Representation for Discovery in Multiscale Physical Fields
likes.summary: The ScaleAware-JEPA framework constructs dense, label-free latent representations for continuous scalar fields by explicitly integrating multiscale organization into self-supervised learning. Applying this method to diverse physical fields like MHD turbulence and galactic molecular gas reveals coherent structural atlases, enabling data-driven discovery without predefined labels.

likes.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning
likes.summary: WORLDEVOLVER introduces a self-evolving world model framework for LLM agents that improves predictive accuracy and planning success by dynamically updating external episodic and semantic memories, without requiring parameter updates to the base LLM. The framework yields an average improvement in agent success rates by +2.24 points on ALFWorld and +3.33 points on ScienceWorld for the Gemma-4-26B-A4B backbone by employing selective, confidence-gated foresight.

likes.title: Parametric Skills
likes.summary: ParametricSkills introduces a framework that transforms free-form textual skills into model parameters (LoRA adapters) at inference time, addressing limitations of in-context learning for agentic LLMs. This approach enhances skill exploitation by overcoming instruction-following bottlenecks, enables context-free execution, and intrinsically links skill evolution with model learning, leading to improved performance in complex software engineering tasks.

likes.title: OSWorld2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
likes.summary: OSWORLD 2.0 introduces a new benchmark for computer-use agents, featuring 108 long-horizon, multi-application tasks grounded in real-world scenarios. Evaluations using this benchmark reveal that frontier agents achieve only 20.6% task completion, highlighting limitations in sustained planning, state management, and error recovery compared to previous benchmarks.

likes.title: SWE-Together: Evaluating Coding Agents in Interactive User Sessions
likes.summary: SWE-Together is a new benchmark for evaluating coding agents using 109 repository-level tasks derived from real, multi-turn user-agent coding sessions, alongside an anchored, state-conditional LLM user simulator. The benchmark quantifies both final code correctness and interaction quality, revealing that stronger models, such as Claude Opus 4.8 (63% pass@1), require less corrective user intervention (1.38 mean User Correction score).

likes.title: GR2 Technical Report
likes.summary: Meta AI's GR2 (Generative Reasoning Re-Ranker) introduces a framework for integrating Large Language Model reasoning into industrial-scale recommendation re-ranking systems. It achieves substantial improvements in ranking quality, such as +18.7% Recall@1, by addressing challenges like vocabulary mismatch and deployment costs through novel tokenization, distillation, and efficiency optimizations.

likes.title: Xiaomi-GUI-0 Technical Report
likes.summary: Xiaomi-GUI-0, developed by the SeerRay Team, introduces an end-to-end multimodal GUI agent for real mobile environments, utilizing a real-device closed-loop training and evaluation paradigm. The 30-billion-parameter model achieves a 72.0% success rate on the new RealMobile benchmark and 78.9% on AndroidWorld, demonstrating robust performance in complex reasoning and planning.

likes.title: GPC: Large-Scale Generative Pretraining for Transferable Motor Control
likes.summary: GPC introduces a framework for transferable motor control by combining Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ) for discrete skill representation with a GPT-style autoregressive transformer. This system, trained on large motion datasets, generates diverse and naturalistic behaviors, achieving high tracking success rates and enabling robust recovery, while allowing efficient adaptation to new tasks through Conditional Low-rank Adaptation (CoLA).

likes.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search
likes.summary: Xia et al. investigate "context rot," the degradation of LLM agent capabilities with increasing context length in multi-turn, multi-source deep search tasks. The study systematically diagnoses this phenomenon using a novel error taxonomy and evaluates various context management and rot-aware rejection sampling strategies, finding that a combined "Keep Latest with summarization" method provides an optimal balance for mitigation and significantly improves reliability.

likes.title: ShopX: A Foundation Model for Intent-to-Item Fulfillment in Agentic Shopping
likes.summary: ShopX, a foundation model developed by Alibaba Taobao & Tmall Group, unifies intent understanding and item fulfillment for agentic shopping by directly translating natural language into catalog-grounded outcomes. The model achieved improved performance on multi-turn, stateful tasks, outperforming tool-mediated LLM-agent baselines in metrics like item precision and feedback adaptation.
